questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.1 Recognize the value of effective safety and health programs in construction
questions.text: What is the main purpose of an effective construction safety and health program?

answers.text: To prevent injuries, illnesses, and fatalities by systematically finding and controlling hazards
To document hazards after every injury but avoid changing work practices
To shift all safety responsibility from management to workers
To focus only on compliance paperwork instead of jobsite conditions

explanations.a: An effective program helps employers and workers identify hazards, control exposures, and prevent harm before incidents occur. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Construction planning clue: documentation matters, but the goal is prevention through action.
explanations.c: Prevention focus: safety and health programs require leadership, worker participation, and shared accountability.
explanations.d: Accountability review: paperwork alone does not protect workers from active construction hazards.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.1 Recognize the value of effective safety and health programs in construction
questions.text: Which result is a likely benefit of a strong safety and health program?

answers.text: Greater acceptance of uncontrolled hazards when deadlines are tight
Fewer incidents, better hazard control, and improved jobsite communication
Less involvement from supervisors and workers
More unreported near misses because workers fear blame

explanations.a: Practical safety clue: effective programs help maintain protection even under schedule pressure.
explanations.b: Strong programs reduce harm and improve communication, planning, and hazard control. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Training-purpose clue: the program works best when supervisors and workers are actively involved.
explanations.d: Hazard-control review: a strong program encourages reporting and learning rather than fear.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.1 Recognize the value of effective safety and health programs in construction
questions.text: A contractor wants to improve safety performance across multiple projects. What is the best starting point?

answers.text: Focus only on accident response after workers are hurt
Wait for OSHA inspections to identify the most serious hazards
Build a structured program with leadership commitment, worker participation, hazard identification, and hazard control
Buy more signs without reviewing site-specific hazards

explanations.a: Communication clue: response matters, but prevention is the core objective.
explanations.b: Corrective-action review: employers should find and control hazards proactively.
explanations.c: A structured program gives the contractor a repeatable way to manage hazards across projects. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Leadership check: signs can help, but they do not replace a complete hazard management process.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.1 Recognize the value of effective safety and health programs in construction
questions.text: A construction supervisor is reviewing safety program responsibilities. Why should safety and health be planned before work begins?

answers.text: Planning eliminates the need for supervisors to monitor work
Planning is only needed after a citation is issued
Planning makes worker training unnecessary
Construction conditions change quickly, and planning helps anticipate hazards before exposure occurs

explanations.a: Construction planning clue: monitoring is still needed because construction conditions change.
explanations.b: Prevention focus: planning should happen before hazards cause harm or enforcement occurs.
explanations.c: Accountability review: training remains necessary so workers understand hazards and controls.
explanations.d: Pre-task and project planning help crews identify controls before hazardous work starts. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.2 Identify management leadership responsibilities for jobsite safety and health
questions.text: Which management practice supports a positive safety culture?

answers.text: Tracking injuries only to blame workers
Treating safety meetings as optional when work is busy
Encouraging hazard reporting without retaliation and acting on reported concerns
Discouraging reports because they slow production

explanations.a: Hazard-control review: a blame-focused approach can hide hazards and reduce reporting.
explanations.b: Foundation clue: consistent communication is part of leadership commitment.
explanations.c: Workers are more likely to report hazards when management responds fairly and corrects problems. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Risk-reduction note: unreported hazards can lead to injuries, illnesses, and fatalities.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.2 Identify management leadership responsibilities for jobsite safety and health
questions.text: What should leaders do when subcontractors share the same work area?

answers.text: Avoid discussing hazards to prevent schedule delays
Assume each subcontractor’s hazards affect only its own employees
Let each crew set conflicting traffic and access rules
Coordinate responsibilities and controls so one crew’s hazards do not endanger others

explanations.a: Leadership check: coordination reduces risk and can prevent costly disruptions.
explanations.b: Worker-input review: hazards can affect multiple crews in the same area.
explanations.c: Hazard-assessment note: conflicting controls can create confusion and additional hazards.
explanations.d: Multi-employer construction sites need coordination so hazards are recognized and controlled across crews. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.2 Identify management leadership responsibilities for jobsite safety and health
questions.text: Which action shows management leadership in construction safety and health?

answers.text: Providing resources, setting expectations, and holding supervisors accountable for hazard control
Telling workers safety is important but refusing to provide required equipment
Leaving all hazard decisions to the newest worker onsite
Rewarding speed even when crews bypass protective systems

explanations.a: Management leadership means visibly supporting safety with resources, expectations, and accountability. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Site-condition clue: leadership requires resources and follow-through.
explanations.c: Answer boundary: management must ensure competent supervision and hazard control.
explanations.d: Practical safety clue: production pressure should not encourage unsafe work.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.2 Identify management leadership responsibilities for jobsite safety and health
questions.text: On site, a construction supervisor is reviewing safety program responsibilities. A project manager learns that crews are bypassing trench protection to save time. What should management do?

answers.text: Ask workers to be careful while continuing without protection
Stop the unsafe practice, provide proper protection, and reinforce accountability
Remove the worker who reported the concern from the project
Ignore the concern until the end of the shift

explanations.a: Foundation clue: caution does not replace required hazard controls.
explanations.b: Management leadership requires prompt action when serious hazards are identified. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Risk-reduction note: retaliation undermines safety and worker participation.
explanations.d: Communication clue: delay can expose workers to serious or fatal hazards.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.3 Identify worker participation practices that support hazard prevention
questions.text: Which action supports worker participation in a safety and health program?

answers.text: Encouraging workers to report hazards, near misses, injuries, and suggestions without fear of retaliation
Punishing workers for raising safety concerns
Allowing workers to report only after a supervisor approves the wording
Ignoring near misses because no one was hurt

explanations.a: Worker participation helps identify real jobsite hazards and improve controls. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Construction planning clue: retaliation reduces reporting and undermines hazard prevention.
explanations.c: Prevention focus: reporting should be accessible and not unnecessarily restricted.
explanations.d: Accountability review: near misses can reveal hazards before injuries occur.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.3 Identify worker participation practices that support hazard prevention
questions.text: Why are workers important in hazard identification?

answers.text: They should replace all supervisor inspections
They often know task details, changing site conditions, and practical control challenges
They are responsible for correcting every hazard without management support
They need no training if they have construction experience

explanations.a: Practical safety clue: worker input is important, but it complements rather than replaces supervision.
explanations.b: Workers can provide firsthand information about hazards and whether controls work in practice. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Training-purpose clue: employers must provide resources and authority for effective controls.
explanations.d: Hazard-control review: experience helps, but training is still needed for hazards and controls.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.3 Identify worker participation practices that support hazard prevention
questions.text: A crew suggests moving material storage to reduce struck-by exposure near a walkway. What is the best response?

answers.text: Adopt it without checking for other hazards
Wait until an injury occurs before considering the change
Evaluate the suggestion and use it if it reduces risk without creating new hazards
Reject it because workers should not participate in safety planning

explanations.a: Communication clue: suggestions should be evaluated so one hazard is not traded for another.
explanations.b: Corrective-action review: near misses and suggestions should be used for prevention.
explanations.c: Worker suggestions should be considered because they can improve practical hazard controls. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Leadership check: worker participation is an important program element.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.3 Identify worker participation practices that support hazard prevention
questions.text: During training, a construction supervisor is reviewing safety program responsibilities. Which practice helps workers participate effectively?

answers.text: Limiting feedback to annual meetings after projects end
Keeping hazard assessments confidential from the crew
Using only technical language workers do not understand
Providing safety information, training, and a clear process for reporting concerns

explanations.a: Construction planning clue: timely feedback is needed while hazards can still be corrected.
explanations.b: Prevention focus: workers need relevant hazard information to protect themselves.
explanations.c: Accountability review: communication should be understandable to the workforce.
explanations.d: Workers need knowledge and accessible reporting paths to participate meaningfully. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.4 Recognize hazard identification and assessment methods
questions.text: Which information can help assess construction hazards?

answers.text: Production goals alone
Rumors without site verification
Near misses, inspections, worker reports, injury records, safety data sheets, and equipment manuals
Advertising claims from unrelated equipment

explanations.a: Hazard-control review: production goals do not identify specific safety and health hazards.
explanations.b: Foundation clue: unverified information should be checked against actual conditions.
explanations.c: Multiple information sources help identify and evaluate hazards more accurately. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Risk-reduction note: relevant task and equipment information is needed.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.4 Recognize hazard identification and assessment methods
questions.text: A new crane lift will occur near an active pedestrian route. What should the supervisor do before the lift?

answers.text: Assume pedestrians will notice the load and avoid it
Review only the weather and ignore ground activity
Wait until the load is moving to decide where workers should stand
Assess the lift area for struck-by, caught-in, access, communication, and exclusion-zone hazards

explanations.a: Leadership check: workers and pedestrians need controlled access and clear communication.
explanations.b: Worker-input review: weather matters, but ground hazards and traffic also need assessment.
explanations.c: Hazard-assessment note: controls should be planned before exposure begins.
explanations.d: Pre-task assessment helps identify hazards and controls before high-risk work begins. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.4 Recognize hazard identification and assessment methods
questions.text: Which activity is part of hazard identification and assessment?

answers.text: Inspecting the jobsite, reviewing tasks, and identifying conditions that could harm workers
Removing controls to see whether workers notice
Waiting for injuries to reveal hazards
Assuming familiar tasks are always safe

explanations.a: Hazard identification and assessment means finding hazards before they cause injuries or illnesses. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Site-condition clue: testing by exposing workers to hazards is unsafe.
explanations.c: Answer boundary: injury data can help, but hazard identification should happen before harm occurs.
explanations.d: Practical safety clue: routine tasks can still contain serious hazards.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.4 Recognize hazard identification and assessment methods
questions.text: In a real example, a construction supervisor is reviewing safety program responsibilities. When should a job hazard analysis be performed?

answers.text: After OSHA issues a citation
Before tasks with potential hazards, especially when work methods, equipment, or site conditions change
After a serious injury occurs
Never for routine tasks

explanations.a: Foundation clue: hazard analysis should be proactive.
explanations.b: A job hazard analysis helps identify task steps, hazards, and controls before exposure occurs. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Risk-reduction note: post-incident review is useful, but hazard analysis should prevent harm.
explanations.d: Communication clue: routine tasks still need review when hazards are present or conditions change.

explanations.b: Practical safety clue: production goals do not identify specific safety and health hazards.
explanations.c: Multiple information sources help identify and evaluate hazards more accurately. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Training-purpose clue: unverified information should be checked against actual conditions.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.4 Recognize hazard identification and assessment methods
questions.text: During training, a new crane lift will occur near an active pedestrian route. What should the supervisor do before the lift?

answers.text: During the shift, wait until the load is moving to decide where workers should stand
During the shift, assume pedestrians will notice the load and avoid it
During the shift, review only the weather and ignore ground activity
During the shift, assess the lift area for struck-by, caught-in, access, communication, and exclusion-zone hazards

explanations.a: Risk-reduction note: controls should be planned before exposure begins.
explanations.b: Communication clue: workers and pedestrians need controlled access and clear communication.
explanations.c: Corrective-action review: weather matters, but ground hazards and traffic also need assessment.
explanations.d: Pre-task assessment helps identify hazards and controls before high-risk work begins. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.5 Identify hazard prevention and control actions
questions.text: Which hazard control approach is generally preferred when feasible?

answers.text: Eliminate the hazard or substitute a safer method before relying on PPE
Warn workers verbally and leave the hazard unchanged
Accept the hazard if the task is short
Use PPE first and ignore whether the hazard can be removed

explanations.a: Higher-level controls such as elimination and substitution are usually more reliable than PPE alone. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Construction planning clue: warnings alone are weak when serious hazards can be controlled.
explanations.c: Prevention focus: short exposure can still result in serious injury or death.
explanations.d: Accountability review: pPE may be needed, but more effective controls should be considered first.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.5 Identify hazard prevention and control actions
questions.text: A crew must work near an unprotected edge. What is the best control approach?

answers.text: Place a warning sign after work is complete
Use effective fall prevention or protection before workers are exposed
Tell workers to stay alert and work faster
Allow experienced workers to decide whether protection is needed

explanations.a: Practical safety clue: controls are needed before and during exposure.
explanations.b: Serious fall hazards require controls such as guardrails, covers, safety nets, or personal fall protection as appropriate. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Training-purpose clue: attention does not replace fall protection.
explanations.d: Hazard-control review: experience does not remove the need to control fall hazards.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health
questions.objective: 2.5 Identify hazard prevention and control actions
questions.text: What should be done after a hazard control is implemented?

answers.text: Assume it works because it was written in the plan
Remove it once workers become familiar with the task
Verify that the control is working and does not create a new hazard
Stop communicating about the hazard

explanations.a: Communication clue: plans must be checked against actual jobsite conditions.
explanations.b: Corrective-action review: familiarity does not eliminate hazards.
explanations.c: Controls should be evaluated after implementation to confirm effectiveness and identify unintended risks. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Leadership check: ongoing communication supports correct use and maintenance of controls.

questions.name: Managing Safety and Health

questions.text: At a daily briefing, a construction supervisor is reviewing safety program responsibilities. Which example best shows controlling a hazard at the source?

answers.text: Relying only on luck during short tasks
Keeping controls optional when production increases
Using slogans instead of installing available protection
Using guardrails around an opening rather than relying only on workers remembering to avoid it

explanations.a: Construction planning clue: luck is not a hazard control.
explanations.b: Prevention focus: controls must remain effective when workers are exposed.
explanations.c: Accountability review: slogans do not physically control serious hazards.
explanations.d: Guardrails physically control access to the fall hazard and are more reliable than memory alone. This is the correct answer.
